L20: 【8†Lemma 15.55.1.】 An abelian group $J$ is an injective object in the category of abelian groups if and only if $J$ is divisible.
L21: 
L22: Proof. Suppose that $J$ is not divisible. Then there exists an $x \in J$ and $n \in \mathbf{N}$ such that there is no $y \in J$ with $n y = x$. Then the morphism $\mathbf{Z} \to J$, $m \mapsto mx$ does not extend to $\frac{1}{n}\mathbf{Z} \supset \mathbf{Z}$. Hence $J$ is not injective.
L23: Let $A \subset B$ be abelian groups. Assume that $J$ is a divisible abelian group. Let $\varphi : A \to J$ be a morphism. Consider the set of homomorphisms $\varphi ' : A' \to J$ with $A \subset A' \subset B$ and $\varphi '|_ A = \varphi $. Define $(A', \varphi ') \geq (A'', \varphi '')$ if and only if $A' \supset A''$ and $\varphi '|_{A''} = \varphi ''$.
L24: If $(A_ i, \varphi _ i)_{i \in I}$ is a totally ordered collection of such pairs, then we obtain a map $\bigcup _{i \in I} A_ i \to J$ defined by $a \in A_ i$ maps to $\varphi _ i(a)$. Thus Zorn's lemma applies. To conclude we have to show that if the pair $(A', \varphi ')$ is maximal then $A' = B$.

L23: 【8†Lemma 15.22.11.】 Let $A$ be a Dedekind domain (for example a discrete valuation ring or more generally a PID).
L24: 
L25:   1. An $A$-module is flat if and only if it is torsion free.
L26: 
L27:   2. A finite torsion free $A$-module is finite locally free.
L28: 
L29:   3. A finite torsion free $A$-module is finite free if $A$ is a PID.
L30: Proof. (For the parenthetical remark in the statement of the lemma, see Algebra, Lemma 【15†10.120.15】.) Proof of (1). By Lemma 【16†15.22.6】 and Algebra, Lemma 【17†10.39.18】 it suffices to check the statement over $A_\mathfrak m$ for $\mathfrak m \subset A$ maximal. Since $A_\mathfrak m$ is a discrete valuation ring (Algebra, Lemma 【18†10.120.17】) we win by Lemma 【10†15.22.10】.
L31: 
L32: Proof of (2). Follows from Algebra, Lemma 【19†10.78.2】 and (1).
L33: Proof of (3). Let $A$ be a PID and let $M$ be a finite torsion free module. By Lemma 【20†15.22.7】 we see that $M \subset A^{\oplus n}$ for some $n$. We argue that $M$ is free by induction on $n$. The case $n = 1$ expresses exactly the fact that $A$ is a PID. If $n > 1$ let $M' \subset A^{\oplus n - 1}$ be the image of the projection onto the last $n - 1$ summands of $A^{\oplus n}$.
